messages.author: df2011c04ce6269d
messages.subject: ANN: A python script for cmdStan
parts:
I saw PyStan run into problems frequently, so I think this script as organized workflow is convenient for other pythoners.

https://github.com/t3476/Python-Kits-CmdStan

only one file cmdStanKit.py is needed.

what it do now:
separate different files: data, sampling output and executables. convenient for cleaning
skip unnecessary compilations
a simple stan_rdump, avoiding GPL issue
sampling leverages all cores and merges outputs into one file
skip noisy outputs on screen and only show when compiling errors happened.

future roadmap:
add more options to sampling
count several kinds of warnings and decide whether it's serious enough. suspend if any kind of warnings is too many
diagnose workflow

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ANN: A python script for cmdStan
parts:
Thanks. I should've read more closely.

We were torn between embedding more deeply and
by calling CmdStan remotely. The other big advantage
is that calling it in a separate process can't tank
your Python process!

I appreciate a license that's more liberal than GPL.

I'd be careful about skipping noisy outputs in case they're
needed somewhere for diagnosing an issue. Maybe a flag to
make output verbose or terse. We're working on getting
things perfectly silent --- some of the prints got away from
us and we're reeling them back in.

- Bob
